ai.description: *Minervarya sengupti* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct dark-spotted flanks. It features a prominent, continuous mid-dorsal ridge and lacks a vocal sac.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya sengupti* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white mid-dorsal line running from the snout to the vent, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya sengupti* inhabits the leaf litter of moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Sengupta's frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter and moist soil of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya sengupti* breeds during the monsoon season, laying clutches of approximately 200–300 pigmented eggs in shallow, temporary water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya sengupti* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya sengupti* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched metallic chirps, typically heard from vegetation near temporary monsoon pools.
